examples.title: Basic select
examples.description: Native select with label and bound string value.

examples.title: Select with disabled option
examples.description: Individual options can be marked disabled.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { Select } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  const options = [
    { value: 'free', label: 'Free' },
    { value: 'pro', label: 'Pro' },
    { value: 'enterprise', label: 'Enterprise (contact sales)', disabled: true },
  ];

  let plan = $state(options[0]?.value ?? 'free');
</script>

<Select id="plan" bind:value={plan} {options} label="Plan" />

examples.title: Typed options with as const
examples.description: Use `as const` on the options array to infer a precise literal-union type for `T`. TypeScript then rejects any `value` that is not a member of the union at compile time.

examples.title: Select with an error
examples.description: A required Select whose placeholder is still selected is invalid: pass a non-empty `error` string to mark it. The control gets `aria-invalid="true"`, the message is wired via `aria-describedby`, and a danger ring replaces the focus ring when the invalid control is focused.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { Select } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  // A `disabled` placeholder paired with `required` is the accessible pattern for
  // a "must pick one" Select: the empty value can be the initial state but cannot
  // be re-selected, and native constraint validation agrees with the `error` prop.
  const options = [
    { value: '', label: 'Select a plan…', disabled: true },
    { value: 'free', label: 'Free' },
    { value: 'pro', label: 'Pro' },
    { value: 'enterprise', label: 'Enterprise' },
  ];

  let plan = $state('');
</script>

<Select
  id="plan-error"
  bind:value={plan}
  {options}
  label="Plan"
  required
  error="Choose a plan to continue."
/>

examples.title: Ghost variant in a bordered row
examples.description: variant="ghost" has no border or fill at rest, a neutral tint on hover and while open, the quiet focus ring around the whole control, and keeps its chevron. Inside a bordered container the controls align to the composer’s 10px text inset and read as one surface. At phone width the row wraps, and a control that still does not fit shortens its value with an ellipsis instead of running past the border.

examples.title: Permissions select with help under each option
examples.description: A ghost listbox select. The current option carries a check, its help sits under it, and the control keeps its tint and quiet ring while open.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { Select } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const permissions = [
    {
      value: 'asks',
      label: 'On changes asks',
      description: 'Tools set to On changes ask before they run.',
    },
    {
      value: 'all',
      label: 'Allow all',
      description:
        'Skips the On changes asks for this chat. Tools set to Always still ask; Blocked tools stay blocked.',
    },
  ];
  let permission = $state('asks');
</script>

<Select
  id="permissions"
  label="Permissions"
  labelVisible={false}
  presentation="listbox"
  variant="ghost"
  size="sm"
  options={permissions}
  bind:value={permission}
/>

examples.title: Agent picker: descriptions, notes, an unavailable group and a footer
examples.description: A ghost listbox select. Each agent has a name and a one-sentence description; model agents show "Needs a provider" while none is connected; agents held back by a disabled plugin sit under "Unavailable" with the reason and cannot be picked; the one link is a footer outside the listbox with its own focus stop.

examples.title: Model select grouped by provider
examples.description: One select grouped by provider. Anthropic lists its models with abilities under each name and a check on the chosen one; providers that are not connected keep a heading with non-selectable text and a link. Closed, the trigger reads the model and its provider.

examples.title: Model select: loading and error
examples.description: While models load the trigger shows its placeholder ("Loading models") and does not open. A listbox select takes the same error prop as the native one: red message, aria-invalid and aria-describedby.
